title: Fast insertion arbitrarily close to bucketized-cuckoo thresholds
formal: For every bucket capacity b≥1 and rational 0<ε<c_b, is there a uniform randomized insertion algorithm that fills a two-choice cuckoo table to load c_b−ε in expected amortized time bounded by an explicit function of b,ε alone, with failure probability tending to zero as table size grows?
definitions: There are m buckets of capacity b. Each distinct key independently receives two independent uniform bucket indices in [m], allowing the indices to coincide. A legal placement assigns each key to one of these indices with at most b keys per bucket. Define c_b=sup{ρ∈[0,1]: a random instance of floor(ρbm) keys admits a legal placement with probability tending to one as m→∞}. Fix b and rational ε∈(0,c_b). Insert N=floor((c_b−ε)bm) distinct keys, in a fixed order independent of all hashes. The algorithm learns a key and its hash pair only when it arrives; it may relocate old keys but may not change hash pairs. After each successful insertion all keys must occupy legal buckets; no stash outside the table is allowed. It may instead report failure and stop. For fixed b,ε the probability of any failure in the N insertions must be o(1) as m→∞, over hashes and private coins. All work including failed insertions is counted. Require initialization O(bm), workspace O(bm), and expected total insertion work at most N f(b,ε) for all sufficiently large m, where f is an explicitly supplied computable finite bound. Each bucket probe, key comparison and O(log(m+2))-bit RAM operation is charged; scanning a bucket costs O(b). Hash indices are supplied at unit cost per key. No deletion support, worst-case insertion guarantee or adaptive key adversary is asserted.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proof of the specified correctness and resource guarantees, or prove that this precise target is impossible. Any conditional impossibility must explicitly state its hypothesis and the implication proved. A theorem with a fixed excluded neighborhood of c_b does not establish every ε>0. A bound depending on m or uncharged retries does not suffice.
context: Bell and Kuszmaul reach a range very close to the orientability threshold, but their stated relative-gap parameter has the lower cutoff δ≥0.99^b.
why: This isolates the algorithmic gap between feasible hash-table load and efficient insertion.

import_provenance.original_title: Fast insertion arbitrarily close to bucketized-cuckoo thresholds
import_provenance.original_statement: For two-choice cuckoo hashing with bucket capacity b, obtain insertion time bounded independently of table size throughout the feasible load range below its sharp orientability threshold, with explicit dependence on the distance to that threshold. This is an editorial theoretical extension of Sanders’s space-efficient bucketized hash-table work.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Later progress: Bell and Kuszmaul’s July 2026 preprint gives an insertion procedure with table-size-independent expected time for loads 1−(1+δ)ε*, where ε* is the threshold slack and δ≥0.99^b, and O(1) amortized expected evictions. This covers a substantial near-threshold range; it is not a claim that every remaining parameter regime or the traditional random-walk rule is settled.

sentences: Each key has two independent random candidate buckets.
Every bucket can hold b keys and insertions may evict older keys.
The target covers every fixed positive gap below the placement threshold.
Time is expected amortized and all unsuccessful work counts.
Failure over the entire insertion sequence must vanish as table size grows.
